pr_title: analyze: introduce --instance= option to control instance name for template units

issue_context.title: `systemd-analyze verify` doesn't handle template units properly
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

256.1

### Used distribution

NixOS 24.11pre

### Linux kernel version used

6.6.36

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

aarch64

### Component

systemd-analyze

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

`systemd-analyze verify` shouldn't fail verifying `systemd-growfs@.service`

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

```
$ systemd-analyze verify  /usr/lib/systemd/system/systemd-growfs@.service 
systemd-growfs@i.service: Failed to create systemd-growfs@i.service/start: Unit i.mount not found.
```

Note that it does work if you fill in the template:

```
$ systemd-analyze verify  /etc/systemd/system/systemd-growfs@-.service
```

### Steps to reproduce the problem

```
#  SPDX-License-Identifier: LGPL-2.1-or-later
#
#  This file is part of systemd.
#
#  systemd is free software; you can redistribute it and/or modify it
#  under the terms of the GNU Lesser General Public License as published by
#  the Free Software Foundation; either version 2.1 of the License, or
#  (at your option) any later version.

[Unit]
Description=Grow File System on %f
Documentation=man:systemd-growfs@.service(8)

DefaultDependencies=no
BindsTo=%i.mount
After=systemd-repart.service %i.mount
Conflicts=shutdown.target
```

### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

_No response_

review_comments: Hmm, I don't grok this? Why not just specify instance in unit id? I think the solution is to give a hint that some units might have restrictions on instance name, but no more?

Of course, `systemd-analyze verify systemd-growfs@.service --instance=tmp` and `systemd-analyze verify systemd-growfs@tmp.service` are equivalent.

But, `--instance` may be useful for passing multiple units in a directory. E.g.
```
systemd-analyze verify /usr/lib/systemd/system/*.service --instance=hoge
```
Otherwise, users need to append instance name to each service name.

Probably. Though I doubt that people really want to inspect so many units at once.

btw, for new code i'd always use strdup() memory for such arg_xyz strings, rather than point directly into argv[]. That's because we nowadays change argv[] in rename_process() at so many places, for example in safe_fork(), which unexpectedly then changes these strings. Hence, given we only duplicate a very small number of strings when parsing command lines, i#d always strdup() this, just to avoid confusion later on (because it is *very* confusing, if various arg_* strings become invalid after safe_fork())
